tables.head: Year listed as a heritage site
rows: Mohenjo-Daro was one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley civilisation and was the first planned city in South Asia. Located on the banks of the Indus River, it flourished between 2,500 and 1,500 BCE. The city was mostly built with baked bricks and followed a strict grid plan.
An ancient city of Gandhara with Buddhist monasteries and stupas and the ruins of three cities (Bhir Mound, Sirkap and Sirsukh); a famous centre of learning from about the 5th century BCE.
Buddhist ruins at Takht-i-Bahi and the remains of Sahr-i-Bahlol
A hilltop Buddhist monastery of the 1st century CE near Mardan, with the ruins of the nearby fortified city of Sahr-i-Bahlol.
Fort and Shalamar Gardens in Lahore
Lahore Fort, a royal fort of the Mughals, and the Shalamar Gardens, laid out by Shah Jahan in 1641 to 1642, are masterpieces of Mughal building and garden design.
One of the largest burial grounds in the world, with about a million tombs of kings, saints and nobles of the 14th to 18th centuries.
Dentistry, at the dental college in Calcutta
Dentist, social worker and political leader (Madar-e-Millat)
